title: Marriage at 18, poverty and nine children
summary: Marriage, a one-room home, working at the Roma Cafe, children and grandchildren.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When did you get married with me?
That would mean about the time of the Depression then?

Yeah. I was staying in one room, five dollars a month. Five dollars a month? There was a room about this size. There was no electricity. The water was in the back. Had a number three tough to take a bath in. You had to wash everything by hand. You know, it was a washboard deal. And the voice ball was born in the house there. On Barracks and Liberty. I'll never forget that. At the time I was playing on Decatur Street at the Roman Cafe.
What year would that be when you went to Roman? 19...
You had to wait a while then in those years before you hadn't been a kid. Yeah, no, gee. Let's see. We had nine kids all the time. That's a lot. This set of twins in there.

Really, it's been a struggle but I enjoyed every bit of it. I don't know. You know, raising kids. Now we have about 24 grandchildren. So, I think, you see they're expecting another one around January. Which would be about 25. So, like I said, it's all in the game.
